_about: Sunday 4 Oct configuration for tools/factory.py. Data only: change this file, not the code; each keeper re-reads it before every start. A 'todo' field marks a value that is still open: `plan` prints every one under its command, and docs/plans/sunday-preflight.md wants none left at 08:40. Placeholders: {python} {until} {params} {duel_ticks} {idle_ticks} {config} {date}. Gates doors_open and clock_running default to true; only the keyless feed and the watchdog opt out. Processes are matched by script basename plus mode token. The dealer bots are on (PR #35 and its follow-up #38 merged: duel lock checked before every accept, pause-safe waits, distinct exit statuses); a dealer step that exits non-zero, or exits 0 without a deal or nothing-to-do marker max_attempts times (default 3), is not relaunched. Dealer commands come from section 7 of the Saturday dealer audit.
pace_assumed_note: Display only: the game hours per wall hour that `plan` assumes before the keepers have measured the running clock (Sunday's published table, Madrid time, fits about 2.0). No gate, no launch and no restart ever reads it.
notify_cmd_howto: notify_cmd stays null until Thiago sets it on the Mini (the one line is in docs/plans/sunday-night-handoff.md): an argv list; the alert text is appended as its last argument and the factory gives it no secrets, so it must read its own token (the Mini keeps it in ~/.config/telegram-notify.env, which tools/mini/tunnel-agent.sh already uses).

processes.name: feed
processes.note: Keyless public recorder; one copy is enough, so the bus claim stops a second machine from starting it.

processes.name: broker
processes.note: Reads its own key from ~/.bazaar/broker.env (--key-file default). The Market Tests (game hours 14.65 hard, 15.0, 17.0, 19.0, 21.0) come from the schedule; status alerts on any dropped match or no match in a test. --policy stall all day (decided Sunday morning: the maxpairs policy lost everywhere it was tested); it is the stall's exact rule.

processes.name: duel
processes.note: The params file is Sunday's own (docs/duel-lab/duel-params-duels3.json, PR #72): never overwrite it with an older Duels II set. One run per wave (Duels III, then the Final): --duel-ticks comes from the schedule event (12 for both) and flags win over the JSON; --late-poll 4 is the 15 s value from the duel audit; --idle-ticks is the window at 15 s ticks and --until the day's close plus 5 min. The window (165 game min) outlasts a wave even if the game clock runs two game hours per wall hour (216 ticks = 108 game min) and closes before the Final's own window opens (21.483 h), so the two never overlap and a crash is relaunched in either wave.

processes.name: abuela
processes.note: On since #35 and #38 merged (duel lock checked before every accept, pause-safe waits, distinct exit statuses). A step counts as done only on a deal or a nothing-to-do line in this dealer's log. No run is LAUNCHED from 25 game min before a duel wave until its configured end (duel_quiet_min and duel_wave_hours: Duels III 1.7 game h, the Final 0.9), whatever the state of the duel lock, which also holds launches while it is fresh. A run launched earlier may still overlap a wave if cooloff waits or several target threads pile up; the dealer_client accept lock (results/duel.lock) then holds its accepts.

steps.label: r3-a1-ret-uncommons
steps.note: RET uncommons are first copies worth 22.5 (book 25 x RET 0.9): cap 22 is the ceiling, strictly inside value. Saturday closes: 22 or less in 20 of 45 deals, 23 or less in 32 of 45. Each one is also the stock for a Pilar resale (L3). Replaces r3-slots-1-3, whose SAL-05 is already ours (plan_empty).

steps.label: r3-a2-ret-commons
steps.note: Fills the L1 slots a1 could not (best three count, the 4th earns about 0). RET commons are worth 9.0, so a close at 9 sits ON the gate: if ladder_points does not move after the first one, drop this step. Closes: 9 or less in 30 of 46, 8 or less in 4 of 46.

steps.label: r3-c1-sal10-fallback
steps.note: OFF by design: Only the one rare Chato sells inside our value (SAL-10 = 70 x 1.3 = 91). Expected credit 0.4 for 86 to 91 P, and it completes the SAL page WITHOUT the page bonus a team trade pays (+3 to +5 points). Enable only if no team has offered SAL-10 by about 11:20 and Hector declines the team buy. Replaces r2-fill-lav09 / r3-slot-1-rare / r3-slots-2-3: LAV-09, SAL-09 and LAV-10 are already ours, so those targets give an empty plan and the factory would mark them done without a trade.

steps.label: r3-c2-sell-cha-uncommons
steps.note: OFF by design: Chamberí only, by hand once a CHA uncommon is ours and no CHA fan has bid for it: CHA uncommon is worth 12.5 to us, Chato bids about 14 (13 to 16). L2 slot at about +0.5 each. Needs the copy to be spare or the last one named (sell:<REF> + --allow-single).

steps.label: r3-l1-resell-ret-rares
steps.note: Resells the two RET rares bought from Los Picaros (value 63.0, floor 64). She loves RET: a thread on Saturday ran 61, 63, 66, 70, 74, 78. A ref we do not hold yet is skipped; an empty plan counts as done, which is why the retry below exists.

steps.label: r3-l2-resell-ret-uncommon
steps.note: The third L3 slot: one RET uncommon bought from Abuela at 22 or less (value 22.5), sold at 23 or more. Her RET uncommon finals on Saturday were 24 to 26 on long threads.

steps.label: r3-l3-resell-ret-rares-retry
steps.note: Same line later: picks up rares that Los Picaros delivered after the first Pilar step found nothing to sell. Empty plan = done, harmless.

steps.label: r3-l4-resell-ret-uncommon-retry
steps.note: Same line later (it falls after the Duels III window and waits for the gates). Only worth running while Pilar has fewer than three deals this round.

steps.label: r3-cha-sell-uncommons
steps.note: OFF by design: Chamberí, by hand: a CHA uncommon is worth 12.5 to us (book 25 x 0.5); she pays about 16 to 21 for sets she does not love. Use after the CHA fans had their chance (docs/plans/ladder-sunday.md section 5).

steps.label: r3-cha-sell-rares
steps.note: OFF by design: Chamberí, by hand: a CHA rare is worth 35 to us (70 x 0.5); she opens about 47 and ends 50 to 56 for sets she does not love. A CHA fan should pay more: try them first.

steps.label: r3-cha-sell-epic
steps.note: OFF by design: Chamberí, by hand: a CHA epic is worth 90 to us (180 x 0.5); she paid 140 to 199 for epics on Saturday.

processes.name: picaros
processes.note: New dealer: agent/chato.py --dealer picaros buys rares from Los Picaros and never sells him anything. A step counts as done only on a deal or a nothing-to-do line in logs/picaros/<date>.jsonl. Same gates as the other dealers. No run is LAUNCHED from 25 game min before a duel wave until its configured end (duel_quiet_min and duel_wave_hours: Duels III 1.7 game h, the Final 0.9), whatever the state of the duel lock, which also holds launches while it is fresh. A run launched earlier may still overlap a wave if cooloff waits or several target threads pile up; the dealer_client accept lock (results/duel.lock) then holds its accepts.

steps.label: r3-p1a-ret-09
steps.note: RET-09 is a first copy worth 63.0 (70 x 0.9): cap 62. He opens at 73 and falls to a final at 52 to 63 as we move (62 or less in 47 of 52 Saturday deals; steps of 1 to 2 P ended at 52 to 57). The rare is resold to Pilar at 64 or more (L3). One card per step on purpose: a run that fills RET-09 and then meets a cooloff on RET-10 exits 0, and the factory would mark a two-card step done with one card bought; as two steps each is judged on its own card (a no-deal run is retried up to 3 times, then fails loudly).

steps.label: r3-p1b-ret-10
steps.note: Same as r3-p1a for RET-10 (also worth 63.0, resold to Pilar at 64 or more).

steps.label: r3-p2-sal10
steps.note: OFF by design: The third L4 slot, and the only one: SAL-10 (value 91) at 62 or less is inside value (about +0.6), but it completes the SAL page without the page bonus a team trade pays (+3 to +5 points, Saturday: LAT-09 at 88 gave +3.10). Enable only if no team offers SAL-10 by about 11:20 and Hector declines the team buy.

processes.name: rastro_seller
processes.note: Off: 232 listings and no fill on Saturday. --step-ticks 40 keeps the 10 min step-down at 15 s ticks.

processes.name: market_desk
processes.note: Page mode: SAL-10 from a team, El Rastro only, bid 80 -> 110 over 64 ticks (docs/plans/pages-sunday.md). The --page flags come from PR #70 (merged). FALLBACK only if a checkout still lacks them: `grep -c 'add_argument("--page",' agent/market_desk.py` prints 0 at 08:00 (the desk would crash-loop on unknown flags): replace this cmd with `python3 agent/market_desk.py run --no-team-venues --no-bids --min-cash 40 --until 15:05` (plain buys only, no page bid; as a list: ["{python}", "-u", "agent/market_desk.py", "run", "--no-team-venues", "--no-bids", "--min-cash", "40", "--until", "{until}"]) or set enabled to false. Starts at 09:00, not after the allowance: cash 253 covers the 110 cap, the dealers get +150 at 10:40. No other bids (--no-bids). Every Chato and Picaros SAL-10 step stays off: a second copy is worth 22.75.

processes.name: matchmaker
processes.note: Keyless writer (public GETs only; it respects the Market Test silence itself): who needs which card, rebuilt every 2 min, from 08:55 so the board is ready when the doors open. The announcer and outreach read logs/matchmaker/latest.json and refuse it when it is older than 15 min; the log column of `status` is that file's age. --census makes holders facts when the census (pre-flight check 12) has run, and falls back to the feed inference when it has not; --exclude-from hides every page card we lack, read from our freshest account snapshot (me_snapshot keeps it fresh); a snapshot older than 90 game minutes pauses the page-card matches.

processes.name: announce
processes.note: KEYED (broker key from ~/.bazaar/broker.env): one missing-card match per public post every 12 min, from the matchmaker's file, each offer re-read in its book right before the post. It carries its own Market Test silence gate (#64) and posts nothing without a fresh file or a match. Keyless dry run: python3 tools/announce.py plan --variant missing. The cards we lack come from the same account snapshot (--exclude-from), not from the hard-coded list.

processes.name: outreach
processes.note: OFF until a human flips it, after the 09:05 test thread (python3 tools/outreach.py run --yes --max-teams 1) shows that a team lists, accepts or trades the named card within 40 ticks (logs/outreach/<date>.jsonl names team and card). KEYED. Each run opens one thread at a time, sends one message, closes it, at most one thread per team per day and never within 2 ticks of a Market Test silence; as a service it runs again after each exit, so only new teams are messaged.

processes.name: me_snapshot
cmd: while true; do {python} -u tools/snapshot.py --me-only || exit 1; sleep 600; done
processes.note: KEYED, one GET /api/me every 10 min: keeps logs/state/me.json fresh (our holdings) for the matchmaker's and the announcer's --exclude-from, and for the VM through logs_push. A failed snapshot ends the loop, so the keeper restarts it (5 s up to 120 s) and status flags a crash loop after 3 failures.

processes.name: logs_push
processes.note: Keyless, never calls the game: mirrors logs/ into the worktree .logs-push on branch mini/logs and pushes it every 10 min (the VM analyst reads that branch). Never touches main. One line per cycle in its window: pushed <sha> <n files>, nothing new, or push failed: <reason> (the loop goes on; see docs/plans/sunday-preflight.md).

processes.name: watchdog
processes.note: Runs status every 60 s and calls notify_cmd when the problem list changes.
